vars.label: Median land surface temperature, summer mornings (Landsat, °C)
vars.ref: USGS Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature (ST_B10) and QA_PIXEL, 244 scenes of June to September 2024-2026 with less than 70% cloud cover, read from Microsoft Planetary Computer at 60 m; the median of each cell's clear views
vars.definition: The median of the land's surface temperature over the area: half the land is hotter. Land surface temperature is the radiative temperature of the ground, roofs, pavement and tree canopy, measured by the satellite's thermal infrared sensor; it is not the air temperature, and on a sunny morning a dark roof or a parking lot can be 20 °C or more above the air. Landsat passes at about 10:30 local time, so these are mid-morning values on clear days of June to September 2024-2026, not the afternoon peak or the night. Each 60 m cell's value is the median of its cloud-free views (at least 3; the typical cell has 30), so a cloud edge the quality flags miss moves it little. A cell belongs to the barrio that holds its centre; a municipio's and Puerto Rico's figures pool the cells of their barrios. Water is left out. Elevation matters: the Cordillera is cooler than the coast, so compare places at similar heights.
